hyperbole can be used to express attitudes, to present the speakers as emotionally involved, and to construct an intended image of the speaker.

hyperbole is a means of discourse that is used in the service of interpersonal rhetoric to convey the speaker's attitude or emotional relation towards the topic of discourse, and to construct a desired impression on conversational partner.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the use of hyperbolic utterance can serve to convey emotional relation to a topic, it also has a social function, which is the construction of an intended impression on interlocutors.
hyperbolic statements are not just exaggerations of facts, but rather serve to express attitudes, which are the main goal of interpersonal communication.

hyperbole can be used for a wide range of discourse goals: to express the speaker's attitude, to present a certain image of the speaker or to construct the image of the speaker in the eyes of the listener.
